I am a farmer here in Quzhou. Forty years on this land, ten mu of it. Let me think how I will do this year.

My land is split between wheat in winter and maize in summer — same as always, same as everyone here. I plant wheat after October, harvest in June, then maize goes in right away and comes out in September. Two crops on the same ground.

For wheat — I always use the improved seed from the dealer in town. Jimai variety, my neighbor Old Wang got 500 kg from it last year, so I trust it. I put down compound fertilizer before sowing, then urea in spring when the wheat starts to green up. Last year I used about 2 bags of compound (50 kg each) per mu as base, then one bag of urea top-dressing. That comes to maybe 18 kg of nitrogen per mu. I water it 3 times — once after sowing, once in spring, once when the head is filling. Wheat needs water or the grain stays small.

For maize — I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan or Xianyu, whatever the dealer has fresh. Maize eats more nitrogen than wheat. I put urea twice — once at the small bell stage, once at the big bell. Maybe 20 kg nitrogen per mu total. Maize roots go deep so I do not water as much, just once or twice if no rain comes. Phosphorus and potassium I put in the compound at sowing — no need to add more, the soil here has enough from years of fertilizing.

Pesticide — wheat I spray once or twice for aphids and rust. Maize I spray once for borer when I see the moths. I do not like spending too much on chemicals.

Tillage — I rent the rotary tiller from the village, everyone does. No-till is for big farms with machines I cannot afford.
